## 1. Background information on the procedure

## 1.1. Type II variation

Pursuant to Article 16 of Commission Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008, Daiichi Sankyo Europe GmbH submitted to the European Medicines Agency on 5 January 2026 an application for a variation.

The following changes were proposed:

| Variation(s) requested   | Variation(s) requested                                                              | Type              |
|--------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|
| C.I.6.a                  | C.I.6.a Addition of a new therapeutic indication or modification of an approved one | Variation type II |

Extension of indication to include the indication first-line treatment of adult patients with unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer for Enhertu (trastuzumab deruxtecan) in combination with pertuzumab is based on results from the phase 3 DESTINY-Breast09 study. As a consequence, sections 4.1, 4.2, 4.4, 4.8, 5.1 of SmPC are updated and the Package Leaflet is updated in accordance. Version 10.1 of the RMP has also been submitted.

## Information on paediatric requirements

Pursuant to Article 8 of Regulation (EC) No 1901/2006, the application included an EMA Decision CW/0001/2015 on the granting of a class waiver for Her-/Epidermal growth factor-receptor antibody medicinal products for treatment of breast malignant neoplasms.

## Information relating to orphan market exclusivity

Pursuant to Article 8 of Regulation (EC) No. 141/2000 and Article 3 of Commission Regulation (EC) No 847/2000, the MAH did not submit a critical report addressing the possible similarity with authorised orphan medicinal products because there is no authorised orphan medicinal product for a condition related to the proposed indication.

## Scientific advice

The MAH received Scientific Advice from the CHMP on 10 December 2020 (EMEA/H/SA/3715/7/2020/II). The Scientific Advice pertained to clinical aspects of the dossier.

## 2. Scientific discussion

## 2.1. Introduction

## 2.1.1. Problem statement

The scope of this variation is to add a new therapeutic indication for Enhertu for the treatment of adult patients with unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer based on the results of the DESTINY-Breast09 study.

## Disease or condition

The MAH initially applied for the following indication:

'Enhertu in combination with pertuzumab is indicated for the first-line treatment of adult patients with unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer.'

## Epidemiology

Breast cancer (BC) is the most common cancer in women worldwide and in the top five-leading causes in cancer-related deaths worldwide (ACS, 2024; Bray et al, 2024). Globally BC represents approximately 12% of all new cancer cases and 24% of all cancers in women with nearly 2.3 million new cases diagnosed and 666,000 deaths in 2022 (ACS, 2024; Bray et al, 2024). By 2040, the burden from BC is predicted to increase to over 3 million new cases and 1 million deaths every year because of population growth and ageing alone (Arnold et al, 2022).

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

In the US, BC is the second leading cause of cancer-related death in women (Siegel et al, 2024). In 2025, the estimated number of women that will be newly diagnosed with BC in the US is 316,950, with 42,170 projected cancer-related deaths in this patient population (ACS, 2025). In Europe, there were an estimated 374,800 new cases of female BC in 2020 and an estimated 95,800 deaths from the disease (European Cancer Information System, 2023).

## Biologic features

Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 positivity is defined as HER2 protein overexpression measured by immunohistochemistry status (IHC3+) or by fluorescence in-situ hybridisation (FISH) measurement of a HER2 gene copy number of six or more or a HER2/CEP17 ratio of 2·0 or greater (Wolff et al. 2013 ASCO guideline). HER2-positive breast cancer comprises approximately 20% of all breast cancers (Wolff et al. 2018, Arteaga et al. 2011).

## Clinical presentation, diagnosis and stage/prognosis

Advanced BC, which includes both locally advanced (inoperable) and metastatic BC, remains incurable. The 5-year survival rate for metastatic BC is approximately 38% (Gennari et al. 2021). Metastatic BC that occurs after previous therapy for early BC, tends to have a more aggressive tumour biology and a worse outcome compared with de novo metastatic BC (Malmgren et al. 2018, Hôlzel et al. 2017). Tumours that overexpress HER2 tend to occur more commonly in younger patients, have a predilection to metastasize to the brain, and are associated with a worse prognosis than HER2-negative tumours (Slamon et al. 1987; Howlader et al. 2014; Parise &amp; Caggiano, 2014; Loibl &amp; Gianni, 2017; Murphy et al. 2019; Bailleux et al. 2021).

## Management

The standard of care in the first line treatment of HER-2 positive unresectable or metastatic breast cancer is pertuzumab in combination with trastuzumab and a taxane (docetaxel or other taxane) (ESMO guideline 2021, Gennari et al. 2021). The superiority of adding pertuzumab to trastuzumab and a taxane treatment was demonstrated in the CLEOPATRA trial, showing a median PFS of 18.7 months and a median OS of 56.5 months in the first-line metastatic setting with this regime (Swain et al. 2015). At a median follow-up of &gt;8 years, there was a 16.3-months improvement in median OS (HR = 0.69; 95% CI: 0.58-0.82 months) associated with the addition of pertuzumab to trastuzumab and a taxane (TPH). This regime is recommended in the first-line setting regardless of hormone receptor (HR) status (estrogen receptor (ER) and/or progesterone receptor (PgR)). For patients with HR-positive and HER2-positive tumours, endocrine therapy (ET) may be added to the trastuzumab and pertuzumab combination as maintenance therapy after completing at least six cycles of concomitant chemotherapy (ESMO guideline 2021).

Although during the last two decades HER2-targeted therapies have improved clinical outcomes significantly, patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer (mBC) will ultimately develop treatment resistance and run out of effective treatments.

## 2.1.2. About the product

Enhertu (trastuzumab deruxtecan, T-DXd) is a HER2-directed antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) composed of a humanized anti-HER2 immunoglobulin G1 monoclonal antibody with the same amino acid sequence as trastuzumab, covalently linked to the membrane-permeable topoisomerase I inhibitor payload DXd via a stable tetrapeptide based linker.

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

In the EU, Enhertu is currently approved as a Conditional Marketing Authorisation (CMA) as monotherapy for advanced HER2+ breast cancer in second or ulterior line of treatment (5.4 mg/kg Q3W), advanced HER2-low breast cancer after chemotherapy (5.4 mg/kg Q3W), advanced HER2low and -ultralow breast cancer after endocrine therapy, advanced NSCLC HER2+ requiring systemic therapy following platinum-based chemotherapy with or without immunotherapy (5.4 mg/kg Q3W), advanced HER2+ gastric or gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma after a trastuzumab-based regimen (6.4 mg/kg Q3W) and other unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive (IHC3+) solid tumours who have received prior treatment and who have no satisfactory treatment options (5.4 mg/kg Q3W).

## 2.1.3. The development programme/compliance with CHMP guidance/scientific advice

This application is based on the phase 3 randomised clinical trial DESTINY-Breast09 (DB-09) which compared the efficacy and safety of T-DXd as monotherapy and T-DXd in combination with pertuzumab versus standard of care Trastuzumab + Pertuzumab + Taxane in patients with metastatic and/or unresectable HER2+breast cancer in the first line setting.

The MAH received Scientific Advice from the CHMP on 10 December 2020 (EMEA/H/SA/3715/7/2020/II). The Scientific Advice pertained to the following clinical aspects: study design for study D967UC00001 (DB-09) including patient population, stratification factors, study endpoints, study treatments and contribution of treatment components, statistical design, interim and final analysis planning.

The Scientific Advice indicated that full blinding of the trial would have been preferable, but accepted an open-label design provided that blinding of pertuzumab versus placebo was maintained within the experimental arms.

While the primary endpoint PFS by BICR (according to RECIST 1.1. in the ITT) was endorsed by the Scientific Advice, the statistical strategy of using a dual primary endpoint was not supported, the reason being that a comparison between the two experimental arms (T-DXd monotherapy and T-DXd + pertuzumab) would be required to fully understand and interpret the study results, as well as to determine the contribution of components.

The Scientific Advice's recommendation on the multiplicity strategy was not followed, as an equal alpha split was advised, whereas an unequal split of 2% for T-DXd versus THP and 3% for T-DXd plus pertuzumab versus THP was implemented.

## 2.1.4. General comments on compliance with GCP

The MAH affirms that this study was performed in compliance with International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) Good Clinical Practice, including the archiving of essential documents.

## 2.2. Non-clinical aspects

No new non-clinical data have been submitted in this application, which is considered acceptable.

## 2.2.1. Ecotoxicity/environmental risk assessment

Trastuzumab deruxtecan is an antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) composed of a humanized anti-HER2 immunoglobulin G1 monoclonal antibody with the same amino acid sequence as trastuzumab, covalently linked to the membrane-permeable topoisomerase I inhibitor deruxtecan (DXd) via a stable tetrapeptide based linker. Antibodies are considered naturally occurring proteins, which are

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

not expected to remain either stable or biologically active in the environment for any significant period. For the cytotoxic payload deruxtecan, the currently approved ERA implemented an Fpen based on a prevalence value for all breast cancer patients, irrespective of disease stage or previous treatments, as a worse case assumption. Therefore, this extension of indication will not result in any increase in the predicted environmental concentration of TDXd, and based on the Guideline on the environmental risk assessment of medicinal products for human use

(EMEA/CHMP/SWP/4447/00 Rev. 1- Corr.*), no updated ERA is required. The justification for not providing an updated ERA is accepted.

## 2.3. Clinical aspects

## 2.3.1. Introduction

## GCP

The Clinical trials were performed in accordance with GCP as claimed by the MAH.

The MAH has provided a statement to the effect that clinical trials conducted outside the community were carried out in accordance with the ethical standards of Directive 2001/20/EC.

## 2.3.2. Methods

## Bioanalysis

There were no changes to the bioanalytical assays for T-DXd, total anti HER2 antibody, DXd, T-DXd anti-drug antibody (ADA), and T-DXd neutralizing antibody (nAb). The same bioanalytical methods used at PPD in the initial marketing authorisation (EMEA/H/C005124/0000) and subsequent BC applications (EMEA/H/C005124/II/0014 &amp; EMEA/H/C005124/II/0022), were used to quantify the analytes in study DB-09. Assay methods to measure T-DXd, total anti HER2 antibody, DXd, pertuzumab, T-DXd ADA, and T-DXd nAb were used to measure these analytes in mainland Chinese patients. The T-DXd, total anti HER2 antibody, and DXd assays at one facility were cross validated against the assays at another facility.

Pertuzumab PK assays were developed and validated before use.

## 2.3.3. Pharmacokinetics

Pharmacokinetics were described by the PopPK analysis based on sparse sampling in the pivotal study DB-09. A non-compartmental analysis (NCA) was not conducted. The study details are described in section 2.4. below.

## PK data analysis

The popPK analysis was performed using nonlinear mixed effects (NLME) modelling methodology as implemented in NONMEM Version 7.5.0 or higher and R Project for Statistical Computing version 4.0.2. or higher. The first-order condition estimation approximation (FOCE) was used as estimation method. The exposure-response analysis was performed using R Project for Statistical Computing version 4.0.2. or higher.

## Population PK modelling

The pre-existing T-DXd and DXd PopPK analysis (based on data from 16 studies) was updated to include data from studies DB-09 (T-DXd + pertuzumab combination arm), DB-07, DB-06, DG-06, DL-03, and DL-05. A PopPK analysis for total anti-HER2 antibody was not conducted because of the

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

similarity to the PK profile of T-DXd. The T-DXd monotherapy arm of study DB-09 was excluded to maintain blinding during the interim analysis and preserve study integrity.

Of the 4007 patients included in the PopPK pool, there were 46767 T-DXd and 46384 DXd PK observations; a total of 320 T-DXd PK samples (0.684%) were below the limit of quantification (BLQ) and a sum of 121 DXd PK samples (0.261%) were BLQ and excluded from the PopPK model. In total, 256 samples (representing ~0.3% of the total number of samples) were considered outliers (defined as those with conditional weighted residuals &gt; 5) and were excluded from the final PopPK model. Of the 4007 patients in the PopPK pool, 2524 (63.0%) had BC, 392 (9.78%) had gastric cancer, 461 (11.5%) had lung cancer, 229 (5.72%) had colorectal cancer, and 401 (10.0%) had other tumours.

Consistent with the previous PopPK analysis, the PK of T-DXd was described by a two-compartment model with linear elimination, while DXd was described by a one-compartment model, with timevarying release of T-DXd. The same covariates as in the previous PopPK model were retained on T-DXd and DXd with the exception of cancer type (colorectal cancer and NSCLC) on clearance of DXd (CLDXd) and cancer type (colorectal cancer) on V3DXd and the addition of concomitant administration of pertuzumab on the central volume of distribution (V1T-DXd), and Japanese ethnicity on the peripheral volume of distribution (V2T-DXd). The impact of these covariates, including concomitant administration of pertuzumab, on the steady-state exposure metrics (AUC, Cmax, and Cmin) remained within bioequivalence ranges (80% to 125%).

The parameter estimates for the final T-DXd and DXd models are reported in the two tables below, respectively. The T-DXd and DXd model were sequentially modelled.

## T-DXd

The concentrations of T-DXd, total anti-HER2 antibody, and DXd were evaluated in the 2 experimental arms in which patients received T-DXd in study DB-09. The focus was to ascertain if there were any significant differences in the concentrations between the 2 treatment arms.

At the DCO (26 February 2025), T-DXd PK data were available for 376 patients in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm A total of 8 patients were excluded from the PK analysis set for T-DXd either because they did not receive study treatment (3 patients) or had no post-dose data (5 patients). No formal NCA was conducted due to the sparse PK sampling scheme in this study.

Samples for T-DXd PK from patients who received T-DXd were collected: pre-dose (within 6 hours before T DXd infusion) at Cycles 1, 2, 4, and 6; post-dose end of infusion (within 15 minutes after

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

## Pertuzumab

Serum concentrations of pertuzumab were measured in the DB-09 study to characterise the PK of pertuzumab in combination with T-DXd. Pertuzumab PK data were available for 152 patients in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm. A total of 229 patients were excluded from the PK analysis set for pertuzumab set either because they did not receive study treatment (1 patient) or had no available post-dose data (228 patients) at the time of DCO.

The trough concentrations (geometric mean) of pertuzumab at Cycle 2 and Cycle 6 were 65.2 µg/mL and 77.9 µg/mL, respectively, which are within the range of historic averages and values reported in the literature (16 to 97 ug/mL [Garg et al 2014]).

## Special populations

The effects of intrinsic and extrinsic factors were investigated using the final PopPK model. The effects of both continuous (Figure 4 and Figure 5) and categorical ( Figure 6 to Figure 9) covariates on steady-state exposure (AUCss) were explored.

## 2.3.4. Pharmacodynamics

## Mechanism of action

Enhertu, trastuzumab deruxtecan, is a HER2-targeted antibody-drug conjugate. The antibody is a humanised anti-HER2 IgG1 attached to deruxtecan, a topoisomerase I inhibitor (DXd) bound by a tetrapeptide-based cleavable linker. The antibody-drug conjugate is stable in plasma. The function of the antibody portion is to bind to HER2 expressed on the surface of certain tumour cells. After binding, the trastuzumab deruxtecan complex then undergoes internalisation and intracellular linker cleavage by lysosomal enzymes that are upregulated in cancer cells. Upon release, the membrane-permeable DXd causes DNA damage and apoptotic cell death. DXd, an exatecan derivative, is approximately 10 times more potent than SN-38, the active metabolite of irinotecan.

## Primary and secondary pharmacology

Primary and secondary pharmacology for Enhertu is described in the initial BC application (see initial MAA EMEA/H/C/005124/0000).

## 2.3.5. PK/PD modelling

Exposure metrics for efficacy and safety analyses were derived from the established DB-09 combination pool population PK (popPK) model of T-DXd.

## Exposure-Efficacy analysis

The exposure-efficacy analyses evaluated the relationship between T-DXd exposure metrics and PFS at the study dosing regimen of T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg in combination with pertuzumab Q3W. All patients from the PK set of the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm in study DB-09 (N = 380) were included in the exposure-efficacy analysis. All PFS events were accounted for, with a total of 118 events in the PK set. Patients were ranked by T-DXd exposure metrics and subsequently classified into four approximately equal-sized groups based on the quartiles of these exposure metrics.

The univariate Cox proportional hazard models did not identify steady state T-DXd exposure metrics (AUC, Cmin, Cmax) as statistically significant factors for PFS (results not shown), thus no further stepwise covariate modelling was performed.

## Exposure-Safety analysis

The exposure-safety analysis was conducted exclusively on BC patients receiving T-DXd + pertuzumab (pertuzumab combination BC safety pool) from studies DB-09 and DB-07. This analysis aimed to assess the relationship between T-DXd and DXd exposure metrics and serious adverse events (SAEs), all Grade interstitial lung disease (ILD), Grade ≥ 3 ILD, all Grade congestive heart failure (CHF), Grade ≥ 3 CHF, all Grade left ventricular dysfunction (LVD), and Grade ≥ 3 LVD. A total of 3010 observations from 430 patients were included in the exposure-safety dataset.

The number of events in SAEs, all-grade ILD, and all-grade LVD within the combination safety pool were 109, 53, and 46, respectively. The number of events in Grade ≥ 3 ILD (3 events), all-grade CHF (5 events), Grade ≥ 3 CHF (no events), and Grade ≥ 3 LVD (9 events) within the combination safety pool (T-DXd + pertuzumab BC Pool) fell below the Pharmacometrics analysis plan (PAP)- specified threshold of 30 events required to perform logistic regression.

The safety endpoints SAE, all grade ILD, and all grade LVD were modelled using the exposure metrics as continuous variables in logistic regression. T-DXd Cmax at cycle 1 was the only exposure metric found to be statistically significantly associated (p&lt;0.01) with the probability of SAE. Stepwise Covariate Modelling (SCM) with the logistic regression model was conducted for SAE. The SCM analysis identified T-DXd Cmax C1 (CMAX\\_TDXD\\_C1), baseline AST (BAST) and age as statistically significant factors, see below table.

## 2.3.6. Discussion on clinical pharmacology

## Methods

The bioanalyses of T-DXd, DXd, ADAs, total HER2- antibody and nAbs have previously been validated. All analyses were conducted according to these methods and the relevant regulatory guidelines. Incurred Sample Reanalysis (ISR) was around the accepted range of 10% of all

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

samples. A method for pertuzumab PK was developed and validated. The validations were carried out according to the ICH M10 guideline and met the necessary requirements. Pertuzumab PK samples were analyzed; however, at the time of DCO, the assay's long-term stability had been established for only 35.58% of the samples. The MAH committed to provide the long-term stability results for the remaining samples post-approval (REC).

A previous monotherapy PopPK model was re-estimated with additional data from studies DB-09, DB-07, DB-06, DG-06, DL-03, and DL-05. The covariates NSCLC and colorectal cancer on CLDXd and colorectal cancer on V3DXd were removed and the pertuzumab combination on V1T-DXd was added. Goodness-of-Fit (GOF) and pcVPC plots indicated that the final model was able to describe T-DXd and DXd data. Of note, a slight underprediction was seen at low T-DXd and DXd concentrations in GOF plots.

## Pharmacokinetics

Pharmacokinetic evaluation was based on sparse sampling in the DB-09 study and subsequent PopPK analysis. T-Dxd PK parameters were determined by an updated PopPK model. The parameters are slightly changed from what is currently included in section 5.2 of the SmPC. However as the DB-09 study's PK parameter results were consistent with prior results with less than 10% difference, and considering the totality of the PK data and the PopPK analysis, there is no clinically meaningful effect of pertuzumab co-administration on the PK parameters of T-DXd. Therefore, no changes to the PK parameters presented in the SmPC are proposed.

## Special populations

The effects of intrinsic and extrinsic factors on T-DXd and DXd exposure were investigated by PopPK modelling. Overall, none of the investigated continuous or categorical covariates are considered to have clinically relevant effect on the exposure of T-DXd or DXd.

No apparent effect of ADA status on T-DXd Ctrough levels was evident with concurrent pertuzumab treatment. Due to the low number of TE-nAb positive participants, no conclusion on the effect on exposure can be made.

## Pharmacodynamics

## PK/PD modelling

The exposure-response datasets included exposure metrics derived from the DB-09 study combination pool PopPK model of T-DXd using individual empirical Bayes estimates (EBEs). In the exposure-efficacy analysis no relationship was identified between exposure and PFS. The exposuresafety analysis was performed on the T-DXd + pertuzumab combination arm data from studies DB-09 and DB-07. Logistic regression was performed. Identified covariates on SAE were T-DXd Cmax at cycle 1, baseline AST and age. Posterior predictions indicated a higher probability of experiencing SAEs at ≥180 ug/mL T-DXd Cmax C1, ≥88 U/L baseline AST, and aged 72 years or older.

## 2.3.7. Conclusions on clinical pharmacology

The pharmacokinetics of T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg Q3W either as monotherapy or in combination with pertuzumab were investigated in the DB-09 study, a phase III, randomised, 3-arm, multi-center, global study. The previous PopPK model was updated.

In conclusion, the PK investigations are considered as supportive for the approval of T-DXd in combination with pertuzumab as first-line treatment in patients with HER2-positive, advanced, or metastatic breast cancer.

## 2.4.2. Main study

DESTINY-Breast09 - Study DB-09: a phase III, open-label, randomized, 3-arm, multicenter, global study assessing the efficacy and safety of T-DXd with or without pertuzumab (blinded for pertuzumab in the T-DXd arms) compared with THP (taxane, trastuzumab and pertuzumab) as first-line treatment in patients with HER2-positive, unresectable, or metastatic breast cancer.

## Methods

Figure 14 Study D967UC00001 (DESTINY-Breast09) Design

<!-- image -->

## Study participants

## Main inclusion criteria

- Patients must be ≥ 18 years of age
- Pathologically documented breast cancer that:
- Was advanced or metastatic (patients who could be treated with curative intent were not eligible)
- Was locally assessed HER2-positive (IHC 3+ or ISH+) according to the ASCO-CAP guidelines based on a tumour sample obtained in the metastatic setting
- Was prospectively centrally confirmed as HER2-positive based on a tumour sample obtained in the metastatic setting
- Was documented by local testing as hormone receptor-positive (either oestrogen receptor and/or PgR positive [oestrogen receptor or PgR ≥ 1%]) or hormone receptor-negative per ASCO-CAP guidelines in the metastatic setting
- Was documented by existing local test result (as per local practice) and/or centrally prospectively assessed as having PIK3CA mutation detected or not detected based on a tumour sample preferably obtained in the metastatic setting
- No prior chemotherapy or HER2-directed therapy for advanced or metastatic breast cancer. One prior line of endocrine therapy is allowed for mBC. Participants who had received chemotherapy or HER2-targeted therapy in the neoadjuvant or adjuvant setting were

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

eligible, with a disease free interval (DFI) from completion of systemic chemotherapy or HER2-targeted therapy to advanced or metastatic diagnosis of &gt; 6 months (&gt; 183 days).

- Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status 0-1.
- At least 1 lesion, not previously irradiated, that can be accurately measured at baseline.
- Adequate organ and bone marrow function within 14 days before randomisation.
- LVEF ≥ 50% within 28 days before randomisation.
- Minimum life expectancy of ≥ 12 weeks at screening.

## Main exclusion criteria

- Contraindications to pertuzumab, taxanes, or trastuzumab per local prescribing information or to T-DXd per the T-DXd investigator brochure (IB)
- History of another primary malignancy except for malignancy treated with curative intent with no known active disease within 3 years before the first dose of study treatment and of low potential risk for recurrence
- Had spinal cord compression or clinically active central nervous system metastases
- Had active primary immunodeficiency, known HIV infection, or active hepatitis B or C infection
- Receipt of live, attenuated vaccine within 30 days prior to the first dose of study drug
- Patients with a medical history of myocardial infarction within 6 months before randomization or symptomatic congestive heart failure (CHF) (NYHA Class II to IV)
- Investigator judgment of one or more of the following:

- QTcF prolongation to &gt; 470 msec (females) or &gt; 450 msec (males)

- History of QT prolongation associated with other medications that required discontinuation of that medication, or any current concomitant medication known to prolong the QT interval and cause Torsades de Pointes

- Congenital long QT syndrome, family history of long QT syndrome, or unexplained sudden death under 40 years of age in first-degree relatives

- History of arrhythmia, which was symptomatic or required treatment (CTCAE Grade 3), symptomatic or uncontrolled atrial fibrillation despite treatment, or asymptomatic sustained ventricular tachycardia
- History of (non-infectious) ILDs that required steroids, had current ILDs, or where suspected ILDs could not be ruled out by imaging at screening
- Lung criteria:

- Lung-specific intercurrent clinically significant illnesses including, but not limited to, any underlying pulmonary disorder

- Any autoimmune, connective tissue or inflammatory disorders where there is documented, or a suspicion of pulmonary involvement at the time of screening

- Prior pneumonectomy

- Prior exposure to antibody drug conjugate that comprises of an exatecan derivative that is a topoisomerase I inhibitor.

All patients treated with T-DXd were to be premedicated with a combination regimen of 2 or 3 medicinal products (eg, dexamethasone with either a 5-HT3 receptor antagonist and/or an NK1 receptor antagonist, as well as other medicinal products as indicated) for prevention of treatment-induced nausea and vomiting.

Participants who developed toxicity leading to discontinuation of T-DXd prior to disease progression could continue treatment on study with trastuzumab 6 mg/kg every 3 weeks (q3w) in either treatment arm. If a participant in one of the experimental arms continued treatment with trastuzumab after discontinuation of T-DXd due to toxicity, the pertuzumab/placebo was continued on the same schedule as trastuzumab. In the THP arm, once the taxane had been discontinued, participants would continue trastuzumab and pertuzumab until disease progression. Endocrine therapy was allowed for patients with HR-positive disease after discontinuation of taxane in the SoC group, or after 6 cycles of T-DXd.

## Outcomes/endpoints

## Primary endpoint

PFS was defined as the time from the date of randomisation until the date of disease progression, as defined by RECIST 1.1, or death (by any cause in the absence of progression) regardless of whether the patient withdrew from randomised therapy or received another anticancer therapy prior to progression (i.e. date of PFS event or censoring - date of randomisation + 1). Patients who

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

had not progressed or died at the time of analysis were censored at the time of the latest date of assessment from their last evaluable RECIST 1.1 assessment. If the patient progressed or died immediately after 2 or more consecutive missed visits, the patient was censored at the time of the latest evaluable RECIST 1.1 assessment prior to the 2 missed visits. If a patient had no evaluable visits, or did not have baseline data, they were censored at Day 1 unless they died within 2 visits from the date of randomisation (12 weeks plus 1 week allowing for a late assessment within the visit window). A NE visit was not considered as missed visit.

In addition, the following supplementary analyses were performed:

- Supplementary Analyses 1 and 2 - Evaluation-time bias

Two separate supplementary analyses using interval censoring methods were performed to assess a possible evaluation-time bias that may be introduced if scans were not performed at the protocol-scheduled time points, where in the first supplementary analysis patients were censored after 2 missed visits and in the second supplementary analysis, patients who progressed or died in the absence of progression immediately following two, or more missed visits were included as events.

Progression or death in the absence of progression was interval censored, where the beginning of the interval was the last evaluable assessment the patient was known to be progression free and the end of the censoring interval was the time of the first assessment where disease progression was detected or time of death (by any cause in the absence of progression). For those patients not experiencing disease progression during the study the PFS time was right-censored at the date of the last progression free assessment.

A log-rank test for interval censored data using Sun's weights stratified by the same stratification factors as in the primary analysis was used to test for a difference in the PFS time between treatment groups.

The HR and its 95% CI and p-value were presented. The HR and CI were estimated from a stratified proportional hazards model for interval censored data using a piecewise constant hazard rate model for the baseline hazard function.

- Supplementary Analysis 3 - Subsequent anti-cancer therapy censoring

The primary analysis for PFS was repeated, but the censoring rule was modified so that patients who took subsequent therapy prior to progression were censored at their last evaluable assessment prior to taking the subsequent anti-cancer therapy.

- Supplementary Analysis 4 - Not applying two missed visits censoring rule

The primary analysis for PFS was repeated, but the censoring rule was modified so that patients who progressed or died in the absence of progression immediately following two, or more missed visits were included as events.

- Supplementary Analysis 5 - Deviation bias

Deviation bias was assessed by repeating the PFS analysis excluding patients with deviations that may affect the efficacy of trial therapy.

## Secondary endpoints

OS was defined as the time from the date of randomisation until death due to any cause regardless of whether the patient withdrew from randomised therapy or received another anticancer therapy (i.e. date of death or censoring - date of randomisation + 1). Any patient not known to have died

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

at the time of analysis was censored based on the last recorded date on which the patient was known to be alive.

The unconfirmed ORR was defined as the proportion of patients with at least 1 visit response of CR or PR and is based on all randomised patients. Data obtained up until progression, or last evaluable assessment in the absence of progression, were included in the assessment of unconfirmed ORR. Patients who received subsequent anticancer therapy after discontinuing study treatment without progression and then responded, were not included as responders in the unconfirmed ORR. Note that, for the derivation of unconfirmed ORR, the following was not considered as a subsequent cancer therapy: 1. radiotherapy and 2. continuing with trastuzumab in cases where T-DXd is discontinued due to intolerable toxicities before the participant has had disease progression. As a sensitivity analysis, confirmed ORR, defined as the proportion of patients with a confirmed response of CR or PR (by BICR according to RECIST 1.1) will also be calculated. A confirmed response of CR/PR means that a response of CR/PR was recorded at 1 visit and confirmed by repeat imaging not less than 4 weeks after the visit when the response was first observed with no evidence of progression between the initial and CR/PR confirmation visit. Data obtained up until progression, or last evaluable assessment in the absence of progression, were included in the assessment of confirmed ORR. Patients who received subsequent anticancer after discontinuing study treatment without progression and then responded were not included as responders in the confirmed ORR (i.e. both visits contributing to a response must have been prior to subsequent therapy for the patient to be considered as a responder).

For patients who achieved at least 1 visit response of CR or PR per RECIST 1.1, DoR was defined as the time from the date of first detection of objective response until the date of documented objective radiological disease progression (using RECIST 1.1) or death in the absence of disease progression (i.e. date of PFS event or censoring - date of first response + 1). The end of response should coincide with the date of progression or death from any cause used for the PFS endpoint. The time of the initial response was defined as the latest of the dates contributing towards the first visit response of PR or CR. As a sensitivity analysis, DoR based on confirmed response was also calculated. For patients who achieved confirmed complete or partial response per RECIST 1.1, confirmed DoR was defined as the time from the date of first documented response (which is subsequently confirmed) until date of documented progression (using RECIST 1.1) or death in the absence of disease progression (i.e. date of PFS event or censoring - date of first response + 1).

PFS2 was defined as time from randomisation until the date of tumour progression on next-line treatment (the earliest of the progression event subsequent to first subsequent anticancer therapy after the first progression) or death from any cause (i.e. date of PFS2 event or censoring - date of randomisation + 1).

## Sample size

Approximately 1620 patients were to be screened/enrolled with an approximate screen failure rate of 30%. Assuming a loss to follow-up of approximately 5% within the first 24 months, the projected number of events at the final progression-free survival (PFS) analysis (approximately 570 events across all 3 arms and at least 395 events for each comparison) was to provide at least 97% power to detect a hazard ratio of 0.70 at an overall 5% alpha level (2-sided test) for the dual primary endpoint (PFS by BICR for T-DXd monotherapy versus THP and T-DXd plus pertuzumab versus THP).

## Randomisation

Randomisation was planned as a 1:1:1 allocation of 1134 patients to T-DXd plus placebo, T-DXd plus pertuzumab, or THP using a centrally managed IRT system. A computer-generated, blocked randomisation scheme was used with separate randomisation lists within each stratum to maintain balance at the central level. Stratification was implemented by prior treatment status (de novo vs recurrent), hormone receptor status (positive vs negative), and PIK3CA mutation status (detected vs not detected), with the proportion of de novo metastatic disease capped at 60%. The realised

## Blinding (masking)

The study was randomised and double blinded for pertuzumab in the experimental arms (i.e. T-DXd + placebo and T-DXd + pertuzumab) by implementing a placebo infusion in the monotherapy arm. An unblinded pharmacist was to prepare all infusions and a secondary, unblinded monitor was to be utilised to perform drug accountability only to enable site and study staff to maintain their blind. In the event of T-DXd discontinuation due to disease progression, the participant proceeded to follow-up and site investigator could request unblinding of pertuzumab/placebo to aid in subsequent treatment decisions. If T-DXd was discontinued for any other reason than disease progression, then upon investigator discretion the participant could or could not continue on trastuzumab. In such case, pertuzumab unblinding was not allowed. Once a participant discontinued trastuzumab due to disease progression, the participant proceeded to follow-up and site investigator could request unblinding of pertuzumab/placebo to aid in subsequent treatment decisions. The Sponsor (except for unblinded monitor) remained blinded until final data readout for the primary endpoint.

The THP control arm was not blinded, though an IRT system was utilised to randomise participants to all three arms. Routines for this procedure were described in the IRT user manual that was provided to each centre. For all study treatments centrally supplied by the Sponsor, IRT provided to the investigator(s) or pharmacists the kit identification number to be allocated to the participant at the dispensing visit. To maintain the integrity of the study, the Sponsor's personnel directly involved in the study conduct did not undertake or had access to the efficacy data aggregated by treatment arm prior to final data readout for the primary endpoint. Before the first participant was randomised, a Trial Integrity Document was generated in which data access levels for relevant Sponsor's personnel were pre-specified.

The blinding could not be broken except in medical emergencies when the appropriate management of the participant required knowledge of the treatment allocation. In this circumstance, the Sponsor's personnel had to remain blinded. The investigator documented and reported the action to the Sponsor, without revealing the treatment given to participant to the Sponsor's staff.

The Sponsor retained the right to break the blinding for SAEs that are unexpected and are suspected to be causally related to a study treatment and that potentially require expedited reporting to regulatory authorities. The blinding was not be broken for the planned analyses of data until all decisions on the evaluability of the data from each individual participant have been made and documented.

## Statistical methods

## PFS by BICR

The dual primary endpoints of the study were progression-free survival (PFS) for the comparisons of T-DXd vs THP and T-DXd + pertuzumab vs THP by BICR according to RECIST 1.1 for patients with HER2-positive mBC. The HR and its 95% CI and the (1-adjusted alpha) % CI were estimated from a stratified Cox proportional hazard modelbased on the same stratification variables as for the log-rank test. The CIs were calculated using a profile likelihood approach. The FAS was used to summarize efficacy data according to the assigned treatment.

KM plots of PFS were presented by treatment arm. Summaries of the number and percentage of patients experiencing a PFS event, the type of event (RECIST 1.1 progression or death) and the number and percentage of censored patients and detailed reason for censoring were provided along with median PFS for each treatment.

The treatment status at progression of patients at the time of analysis was summarized.

This included the number (%) of patients who were on treatment at the time of progression, who discontinued study treatment prior to progression, who have not progressed and were on treatment or discontinued treatment. The distribution of number of days prior to progression for the patients who have discontinued treatment was also provided.

The assumption of proportionality was assessed. Proportional hazards were tested firstly by examining plots of complementary log-log (event times) versus log (time) and, if these raise concerns, by fitting a time-dependent covariate (adding a treatment-by-time or treatment-bylog(time) interaction term) to assess the extent to which this represents random variation. If a lack of proportionality was evident, the variation in treatment effect could be described by presenting piecewise hazard ratios calculated over distinct time-periods. In such circumstances, the hazard ratio can still be meaningfully interpreted as an average hazard ratio over time unless there is extensive crossing of the survival curves. If a lack of proportionality was found, this may be a result of treatment-by-covariate interactions, which was investigated.

An exploratory analysis of PFS by BICR was performed to compare T-DXd+ pertuzumab versus T-DXd. This analysis was performed using the same methodology as for the primary endpoint described above. This was not included in the multiple testing strategy.

## Sensitivity and supplemental analyses

The following sensitivity analyses were performed:

- Stratification factors according to electronic case report form (eCRF) data and central lab data (if applicable).

In the event that there was any mis-stratifications during randomisation, the stratified log rank test was repeated on PFS, where the stratification factors including prior treatment status and HR status were as recorded in eCRF and PIK3CA mutation status was as recorded in central lab data (if applicable). The HR and CI were also presented from the Cox proportional hazards analysis.

## Subgroup analyses

Subgroup analyses were conducted for PFS and OS on the following factors:

- Prior treatment status (de novo vs recurrent)
- HR status (positive vs negative)
- PIK3CA mutation status (detected vs not detected)
- Brain metastases at baseline (present vs not present)

## PFS by Investigator assessment

PFS by investigator assessment according to RECIST 1.1, in the FAS, was analysed as described for the primary endpoint. However, if there were insufficient events per treatment arm in each stratum using the same stratification factors as used in primary endpoint, an unstratified log-rank test and Cox proportional hazards model was performed, as described in the pooling strategy.

When examining the results of the PFS by BICR and PFS by investigator assessment, if there was an important discrepancy between the primary analysis data and the analysis using investigator data, the proportion of patients with site but no central confirmation of progression was to be summarised; such patients had the potential to induce bias in the central review due to informative censoring. An approach of imputing an event at the next visit in the central review analysis could help inform the most likely hazard ratio value, but only if an important discrepancy existed.

Disagreements between investigator and central reviews of RECIST progression were presented for each treatment arm. The summary included the early discrepancy rate (frequency with which the investigator declared progression earlier than BICR within each treatment arm as a proportion of the total number of Investigator-assessed progressions) and the late discrepancy rate (frequency with which investigator declared progression later than BICR as a proportion of total discrepancies within the treatment arm). A tolerance of 2 weeks was considered when comparing the progression dates by BICR and investigator assessment.

## OS

OS was analysed as described for the primary endpoint. However, if there were insufficient events per treatment arm in each stratum using the same stratification factors as used in primary endpoint, an unstratified log-rank test and Cox proportional hazards model were performed, as described in the pooling strategy. The 2-sided 95% CI of hazard ratio was provided. The (1-adjusted alpha)% CI of hazard ratio, and the p value were provided if the OS was formally tested.

KM plots of OS were presented by treatment arm. Summaries of the number and percentage of patients who had died, those still in survival follow-up, those lost to follow-up and those who had withdrawn main consent were provided along with the median OS for each treatment.

The assumption of proportionality of hazards was assessed as described for the primary endpoint.

Censoring patterns with regard to the primary treatment comparisons was assessed by a KM plot of time to censoring where the censoring indicator of OS were reversed. In addition, duration of follow-up was summarised using median time from randomisation to the date of death (i.e., overall survival) or to the date of censoring (date last known to be alive) for censored patients regardless

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

of treatment arm. The same subgroup analyses as described for the primary endpoint were to be presented.

## Sensitivity analyses of overall survival: treatment switching

Exploratory analyses of overall survival adjusting for the impact of treatment switching were performed to inform decision-makers, including payers. Methods such as the rank preserving structural failure time (RPSFT), inverse probability of censoring weighting (IPCW), and two steps methods (Latimer et al. 2014) were to be explored. The final choice of methods was based on numerous factors including, but not limited to, the completeness of data, the degree of treatment switching, maturity of data, whether switching occurs very early or later in the trial, and the plausibility of the underlying assumptions including the constant treatment effect for the rank preserving method and the exchangeability assumption for IPCW and two step methods. If the described methods were deemed to be insufficient to describe the disease and treatment process, other methods may need to be explored. Further details were provided in the Payer Analysis Plan.

## ORR

At the time of any PFS and OS analyses, the unconfirmed objective response rate (ORR) by BICR according to RECIST 1.1 was compared between active treatment (T-DXd or T-DXd + pertuzumab) and THP. A logistic regression model was used to analyse the ORR, adjusting for the same stratification factors as the primary endpoint. The results of the analysis were to be presented in terms of an odds ratio (an odds ratio greater than 1 favours T-DXd + pertuzumab placebo or T-DXd + pertuzumab vs THP) together with its associated profile likelihood 95% CI and p-value (based on twice the change in log-likelihood resulting from the addition of a treatment factor to the model).

The point estimates of the observed ORR without adjusting for any covariates were provided for each treatment arm and their 95% CIs were provided using the Clopper- Pearson exact method. The differences between the active T-DXs treatment arms and THP were reported using point estimates as well their 2-sided 95% CI using the Miettinen- Nurminen method. The ORR based on investigator assessments according to RECIST 1.1 was also analyzed using the same methodology described above as a sensitivity analysis. An exploratory analysis of ORR was performed to compare T-DXd + pertuzumab versus T-DXd using the same methodology described above (based on both BICR and investigator assessments).

As a sensitivity analysis, confirmed ORR, defined as the proportion of patients with a confirmed response of CR or PR (by BICR and by investigator assessments according to RECIST 1.1) was analysed using the same methodology as described above. If there were not enough responses, for a meaningful analysis using logistic regression, then a stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test was presented, with the same stratification factors as used in the primary endpoint analysis.

Summaries were produced that present the number and percentage of patients with a tumour response (CR/PR) based upon:

- the total number of patients in the population and
- the number of patients in the population with measurable disease at baseline per BICR (sensitivity analysis).

For each treatment arm, best overall response (BoR) was summarised by n (%) for each category (CR, PR, SD, PD and NE). No formal statistical analyses were planned for BoR.

## DoR

For the duration of response (DoR), descriptive data was provided (with no confirmation of response required) by BICR and by investigator assessment according to RECIST 1.1 in responding patients, including the associated KM curves (without any formal comparison of treatment arms or p-values attached) and KM estimates. The DoR was based on a subset of patients in the FAS who have achieved objective tumor response.

## PFS2

Time from randomisation to second progression or death (PFS2) was analysed by using identical methods as outlined for the primary endpoint and adjusting for the same set of covariates. The hazard ratio for the treatment effect together with its 95% CI was presented. Medians and KM plots were presented to support the analysis. The number and percentage of patients experiencing a PFS2 event and the type of progression (objective radiological progression, symptomatic progression in absence of objective radiological progression or other) were also summarised by treatment arm, as well as summaries of deaths in the absence of second progression, and categories of PFS2 censoring. Time from randomisation to second progression was summarised by treatment arm.

## Interim analysis

## Futility analysis

A futility analysis regarding PFS by BICR in the FAS was performed when 228 PFS events had occurred within all three arms (standing for 40% of the target PFS events, 20% maturity), with at least 158 events observed from the T-DXd monotherapy and THP arms. This was expected to occur approximately 24 months after the first patient is randomised, assuming a non-uniform recruitment over 24 months.

## Interim PFS analysis

An interim analysis for efficacy regarding PFS by BICR in the FAS was to take place when approximately 399 PFS events had occurred within all three arms (standing for 70% of the target PFS events, 35% maturity), with at least 277 PFS events observed for each comparison. This was expected to occur approximately 32 months after the first patient is randomised, assuming nonuniform recruitment of patients with the duration of 24 months, 18.7 months of median PFS with THP and a hazard ratio of 0.70 between the experimental arms and the THP arm.

## Interim OS analysis

Four interim analyses for OS were planned using stratified log-rank tests in addition to a final analysis for OS, with stratification factors in line with the pooling strategy. The timing of the OS analyses was based on the following assumptions: a median OS of 56.5 months for the THP arm, an average hazard ratio of 0.75 between the experimental arms and the THP arm, and a 20% crossover rate from the THP arm to the experimental arm after progression. Since the first two interim analyses of OS were to be performed at the same time as the analyses of PFS, the number of OS events did not determine the timing of the OS analyses for the first two interim analyses.

OS analyses are as described below:

- The first interim OS analysis was performed at the time of the first interim efficacy analysis for PFS. Approximately 171 OS events (15% maturity or 27% information fraction) are were anticipated to be observed at the time of the first PFS interim efficacy analysis.

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

- The second interim OS analysis will was to occur at the time of the final PFS analysis. It is was anticipated that approximately 254 OS events (22% maturity or 40% information fraction) will would have been observed across the three arms. Since the first two interim analyses of OS will were to be performed when analyses of PFS occur, the anticipated number of OS events at each interim analysis did not determine the timing of the analysis.
- The third interim OS analysis will would take place when approximately 488 OS events had occurred across the three arms (43% maturity or 77% information fraction) and at least 333 OS events had occurred in each comparison. This was anticipated to be approximately 74 months after the first patient is randomized.
- The fourth interim OS analysis will would take place when approximately 571 OS events had occurred across the three arms (50% maturity or 90% information fraction) and at least 390 OS events had occurred in each comparison. This was anticipated to be approximately 90 months after the first patient is randomized.
- The final OS analysis will would occur when approximately 634 OS events have been observed within all three arms and at least 433 OS events have occurred in each comparison. This is anticipated to be approximately 105 months after the first patient is randomized.

For the OS hypothesis, cumulative alpha values of 0.003%, 0.079%, 2.08%, and 3.68% will were spent for the first to the fourth interim analysis, assuming the information fraction of 27%, 40%, 77% and 90%, respectively following the Lan DeMets spending function. The final OS analysis will have a cumulative 5% alpha. Cut-off values for each test in terms of hazard ratios and alpha values are provided in the below table.

Under this procedure, the significance levels at the interim and final analyses were determined by the information fraction available at the time of analysis (i.e., exact number of events observed), assigning greater weights to analyses performed at later time points.

## Multiplicity

To control the overall Type I error at the two-sided 5% level, a Fallback multiple testing procedure (MTP) with a gate keeping strategy was used across the PFS comparisons between T-DXd and THP and between T-DXd + pertuzumab and THP. The study was to be considered successful if either test of PFS was significant. The final PFS analysis was to be performed when approximately 570 PFS events had occurred within all three arms; to maintain the power of each test at the final analysis, at least 395 PFS events should have occurred for each comparison. An initial 2% alpha was used for the analysis of T-DXd versus THP and an initial 3% alpha was used for the analysis of T-DXd + pertuzumab versus THP. The alpha allocated to each PFS test was distributed between the interim and final analyses using the Haybittle-Peto approach. The spent alpha values could be recycled between successfully rejected comparisons for PFS. The significance level at the interim analysis would remain the same but the significance level at the final analysis would be updated based on a 5% overall alpha using the Haybittle-Peto approach. The final OS analysis was to occur when approximately 634 OS events had been observed within all three arms and when at least 433 OS events had occurred in each comparison. OS was tested hierarchically at two-sided 5% alpha if and only if statistical significance was reported for the dual primary endpoints. To clarify, both tests (T-DXd vs THP and T-DXd + pertuzumab vs THP) needed to report statistical significance (see figure below) to move forward with the OS test. The hierarchical OS testing was first for the comparison of T-DXd + pertuzumab and THP and then between T-DXd and THP. The alpha allocated to each OS test was distributed between the interim and final analyses using the LanDeMets alpha spending function with an O'Brien-Fleming type of boundary. The MTP is described in the below figure.

The following is a list of all planned PFS and OS analyses for this study:

1. Futility Analysis - futility criteria based on PFS
2. Interim Analysis - PFS and OS (OS-IA-1)
3. Final PFS Analysis, includes an OS analysis (OS-IA-2)
4. Interim Analysis - OS (OS-IA-3)

## Protocol amendments

All protocol amendments were executed based on either recommendation or advice from regulatory agencies, in response to evolving international clinical practice guidelines, or due to external emerging clinical data. All clinical study protocol (CSP) amendments were made prior to the DCO date of the futility analysis for PFS by BICR in the FAS (20 November 2023), and the Sponsor remained blinded to the data until the PFS interim efficacy analysis/OS IA 1 (DCO: 26 February 2025). A separate blinded team continued the medical monitoring of the patients who are still on the study to maintain the study integrity until the final analysis. The Sponsor study team was responsible for all changes to the planned statistical analyses. All major changes were made prior to the database lock (DBL) for the interim PFS analysis (DCO: 26 February 2025).

The main reason for these protocol amendments was to update certain aspects of the study design, including change in the cap of patients with de novo metastatic disease, and change in method to determine the stopping boundaries for PFS from O'Brien Fleming approach to Haybittle-Peto in order to set a more stringent efficacy boundary at the time of the interim analysis. This protocol was also updated to align with the current project-level requirements for T-DXd study protocols and the EU Directive to EU CTR (Clinical Trial Regulation).

## Recruitment

First patient enrolled: 26 April 2021.

Last patient enrolled: not available.

Data cut-off (DCO): 26 February 2025.

## Countries

Patients were enrolled and treated at 279 centres in 27 countries worldwide: 21.7% in Europe and North America, 49.2% in Asia, and 29.0% in the Rest of World. There were sites in China (35), India (11), Japan (31), Korea (11), Philippines (9), Taiwan (8), Argentina (13), Brazil (10), Israel (6), Mexico (6), Peru (6), Russia (7), Saudi Arabia (6), Turkey (7), South Africa (10), Hungary (10), Romania (3), Belgium (9), Germany (12), Denmark (4), Spain (9), France (16), Great Britain (8), Italy (10), Sweden (6), Canada (14), USA (29).

The interim analysis (IA) of the primary variable of progression-free survival (PFS) by blinded independent central review (BICR) at the data cut-off (DCO) of 26 February 2025 are presented below. All secondary efficacy endpoints were analysed at the time of this analysis.

## Amendments

Several statistically relevant protocol amendments were implemented after recruitment started and before the interim PFS DCO. These included updating key design assumptions such as the target HR to 0.70 and corresponding interim analyses, changing the de novo cap from 50% to 60%, and allowing local PIK3CA results for eligibility and stratification when central data were unavailable. The interim PFS boundary method was amended from an O'Brien-Fleming type approach to Haybittle-Peto to apply a more stringent interim efficacy threshold, and several secondary endpoint details were streamlined or moved to the SAP.

## Confirmed objective response rate (ORR) per BICR

As per BICR assessment, the ORR was 85.1% (95% CI: 81.2, 88.5) in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm and 78.6% (95% CI: 74.1, 82.5) in the THP arm with an odds ratio of 1.59 (95% CI: 1.09, 2.32; nominal p-value: 0.015). PR was achieved in the same proportion of patients (70.0% in both arms) in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm and in the THP arm.

## Duration of confirmed response (DoR)

As of the DCO, the median duration of confirmed objective response based on BICR assessment was longer in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm (39.2 months, 95% CI: 35.1, NC) compared with the THP arm (26.4 months, 95% CI: 22.3, NC).

## In vitro biomarkers test for patient selection for efficacy

In the DB-09 study, HER2-positivity (IHC 3+ or ISH+) was locally assessed according to the ASCOCAP guideline (Wulff et al. 2018) on a tumour sample obtained in the metastatic setting and was prospectively centrally confirmed as HER2-positive using PATHWAY/VENTANA anti-HER2/neu (4B5) and VENTANA HER2 Dual ISH DNA Probe Cocktail. This method of biomarker selection is unchanged since the first approval of Enhertu for HER2-positive (IHC 3+ or ISH+) BC (CHMP assessment report EMEA/H/C/005124/0000).
