## Supportive study

Not applicable.

## 2.4.3. Discussion on clinical efficacy

The MAH submitted the DB-09 study results to support an extension of indication for Enhertu in combination with pertuzumab for the first-line treatment of adult patients with unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer.

## Dose finding and dose recommendation study DB-07

In part 2 of the DB-07 study there were 75 patients in the T-DXd arm and 50 patients in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm. There was a numerically slightly higher proportion with overall response in the combination arm (83% vs. 88%). The proportion of PFS events was slightly smaller in the T-DXd monotherapy arm and the median PFS was not reached in either arm (not alpha-controlled). The median follow-up was approximately 30 months in the T-DXd arm and 36 months in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm. Conclusively, T-DXd monotherapy and T-DXd in combination with pertuzumab has been compared head-to-head in the phase 2 DB-07 study, however the comparison was not based on a formal statistical hypothesis, and thus the results are not alpha-controlled. In the DB-07 study no sound differences in ORR and PFS were observed.

The recommended dose of Enhertu, in combination with pertuzumab, is 5.4 mg/kg body weight given as an intravenous infusion once every 3 weeks (21-day cycle), with approximately 30 minutes between infusions, until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

- Cycle 1, Day 1: Administer 5.4 mg/kg of Enhertu followed by a separate intravenous infusion of pertuzumab at 840 mg.
- Subsequent cycles, Day 1: Administer 5.4 mg/kg of Enhertu followed by a separate intravenous infusion of pertuzumab at 420 mg.

## Design and conduct of clinical studies

The DB-09 study is a phase III, open-label, randomized, 3-arm, multicenter, global study assessing the efficacy and safety of T-DXd with or without pertuzumab (blinded for pertuzumab in the T-DXd arms) compared with THP (taxane, trastuzumab and pertuzumab) as first-line treatment in patients with HER2-positive, unresectable, or metastatic breast cancer.

## Target population

The target population encompasses patients with HER2-positive, unresectable, or metastatic breast cancer (BC), which is either de novo mBC or recurrent BC. Prior treatment in the neoadjuvant or adjuvant setting was permitted, with a DFI from completion of systemic chemotherapy or HER2targeted therapy to advanced or metastatic diagnosis of &gt; 6 months (&gt; 183 days). Patients could have either HR-positive or HR-negative disease and must have ECOG performance status 0-1.

Overall, the population selected by the eligibility criteria appropriately reflects the target population for which the indication is sought with the exception that the DFI in the study population could be at least 6 months instead of 12 months. The current ESMO guideline uses DFI &gt; 12 months, as did the CLEOPATRA trial (which established THP as the SoC in the first line setting for HER2 positive mBC). The current ESMO guideline (2021) suggests that patients with metastatic recurrence within 12 months of receiving adjuvant trastuzumab and pertuzumab should follow second-line therapy recommendations (Gennari et al. 2021). Thus, for this aspect the control THP arm differs from the

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

current SoC and it could be claimed that patients in the control arm with a DFI below 12 months may have received suboptimal SoC in the control arm. However, the proportion of patients with a disease-free interval below 12 months was low (2.1.%) in the combination arm, and this magnitude is not considered to have potential for impacting the overall study results.

## Treatments

The treatment in the control arm is aligned with the standard of care currently recommended in Europe (ESMO BC guideline 2021), i.e. standard first-line treatment of HER2-positive mBC should be a combination of pertuzumab-trastuzumab-docetaxel regardless of HR status and docetaxel should be given for at least 6 cycles or until unacceptable toxicity, followed by maintenance pertuzumab-trastuzumab until progression. An alternate taxane (paclitaxel, nab-paclitaxel) may be given instead of docetaxel and endocrine therapy may be added to the pertuzumab-trastuzumab combination as maintenance after completion of chemotherapy for HR-positive tumours.

The rationale for combining T-DXd and pertuzumab was based on the efficacy results from another study combining pertuzumab with another ADC i.e. T-DM1 (Perez et al. 2017) as well as on preclinical data. The rationale was further based on preliminary data from the DB-07 study, a phase I/II study, in which T-DXd both as monotherapy and in combination with pertuzumab was investigated in HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer (Hamilton et al. 2022). The MAH has provided the final analysis of the DB-07 study. The head-to-head comparison of T-DXd monotherapy versus T-DXd in combination with pertuzumab was not based on a formal statistical hypothesis. In the DB-07 study no sound differences in ORR and PFS were observed. The MAH's rationale for combining T-DXd with pertuzumab, was mainly based on the assumption that, given the efficacy that T-DXd monotherapy has already demonstrated in heavily pre-treated patients, the efficacy would be further improved in early-line patients with the addition of pertuzumab. No prior clinical data demonstrating a superior effect of combining T-DXd with pertuzumab over monotherapy with T-DXd have been submitted in this application. Although the contribution of the components T-DXd and pertuzumab cannot be disentangled due to the lack of a direct comparison to monotherapy T-DXd, the combination therapy in the experimental arm is a substitution of the taxane and trastuzumab combination with T-DXd, while maintaining pertuzumab, and the rationale for this substitution is acknowledged.

Participants who developed toxicity leading to discontinuation of T-DXd prior to disease progression could continue treatment on study with trastuzumab 6 mg/kg every 3 weeks (q3w) in either treatment arm. If a participant in one of the experimental arms continued treatment with trastuzumab after discontinuation of T-DXd due to toxicity, the pertuzumab/placebo was continued on the same schedule as trastuzumab. In the THP arm, once the taxane had been discontinued, participants would continue trastuzumab and pertuzumab until disease progression. Endocrine therapy was allowed for patients with HR-positive disease after discontinuation of taxane in the SoC group, or after 6 cycles of T-DXd. This treatment strategy is considered acceptable and in line with current ESMO recommendations.

## Study design, stratification and endpoints

Blinding of all treatments in each arm would have been the preferable methodology, however, in an overall non-blinded setting, the blinding of pertuzumab treatment as well as BICR assessment of the primary endpoint, are considered acceptable bias-mitigating factors.

The stratification factors at randomisation were 1) choice of prior treatment status (de novo vs. recurrent), 2) hormone receptor (HR) status (HR-positive vs. HR-negative) and 3) PIK3CA mutation status (detected vs. not detected). Patients were randomised 1:1:1. The stratification

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

factors are known to be prognostic for patient outcome and were endorsed by the CHMP during the Scientific Advice.

The primary endpoint PFS was defined as the time from randomisation until disease progression according to BICR (RECIST 1.1.) or death by any cause. The primary endpoint was dual, aiming at establishing 1) the superiority of T-DXd and pertuzumab compared to THP and/or 2) the superiority of T-DXd and placebo compared to THP. The statistical method used was a multiple testing procedure with gatekeeping across the two primary PFS comparisons versus THP, with study success defined by significance of either PFS. The initial two-sided alpha was split with 2% for T-DXd versus THP and 3% for T-DXd plus pertuzumab versus THP. The secondary endpoint OS was to be tested hierarchically, only if both primary PFS comparisons were significant. The comparison between the T-DXd monotherapy arm and the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm is only planned to be an exploratory comparison and not included in the multiple testing procedure.

While the primary endpoint PFS by BICR (according to RECIST 1.1. in the ITT) was endorsed by the CHMP during the Scientific Advice (EMA/CHMP/SAWP/640729/2020), the statistical strategy of using a dual primary endpoint was not supported, the reason being that a comparison between the two experimental arms (T-DXd monotherapy and T-DXd + pertuzumab) would be required to fully understand and interpret the study results, as well as to determine the contribution of the components. The alpha-split 2%/3% between the experimental arms was not supported either, as it would favour the combination therapy if each of the two experimental arms had comparable efficacy, and instead allocation of alpha 2.5% to each arm was recommended. With the strategy chosen by the MAH, the contribution of the components of the T-DXd + pertuzumab vs T-DXd monotherapy, cannot be formally disentangled.

The OS analysis is subject to hierarchical testing at two-sided 5% only if both primary PFS comparisons are significant. This means that analysing OS for the combination of T-DXd + pertuzumab vs THP will only be alpha-controlled if there is a statistically significant improvement in mPFS for both the comparisons versus THP. This approach was not supported by the CHMP during the Scientific Advice, since if only one PFS comparison was positive, it should be possible to make confirmatory conclusions on the corresponding OS result. Other secondary endpoints were PFS assessed by investigator, ORR, DoR and PFS2.

Statistical methods: The primary objective was evaluated as dual primary PFS by BICR for T-DXd versus THP and T-DXd plus pertuzumab versus THP in the FAS, with key secondary endpoints including OS, investigator-assessed PFS, ORR and DoR and PFS2. Randomisation was centrally implemented 1:1:1 via IRT using blocked lists within strata and stratified by de novo versus recurrent status, HR status, and PIK3CA mutation status, which was considered acceptable and was balanced across arms. Blinding was maintained for pertuzumab within the experimental arms using placebo infusion while THP remained open label, and assessment bias was mitigated by BICR for the primary endpoint and a prespecified trial integrity plan with restricted unblinding. PFS censoring rules were prespecified and included specific handling of missed-visit scenarios and Day 1 censoring for patients without evaluable post-baseline data, and robustness was supported by prespecified supplementary analyses addressing evaluation-time bias, alternative missed-visit handling, censoring at subsequent therapy, and deviation bias, which yielded consistent results.

Sample size is event-driven and powered for an HR of 0.70. Multiplicity control was prespecified to strongly control the overall two-sided 5% Type I error using a fallback multiple testing procedure with gatekeeping across the two primary PFS comparisons versus THP, with study success defined by significance of either PFS test and with alpha recycling between successfully rejected PFS hypotheses. The initial two-sided alpha was split as 2% for T-DXd versus THP and 3% for T-DXd plus pertuzumab versus THP, with interim and final boundaries derived using a Haybittle-Peto

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

spending approach for PFS, while OS was protected by hierarchical testing at two-sided 5% only if both primary PFS comparisons were significant, using Lan-DeMets alpha spending with an O'BrienFleming type boundary across planned OS analyses. The CHMP Scientific Advice

(EMEA/H/SA/3715/7/2020/II) recommendation on the multiplicity strategy was not followed, as an equal alpha split was advised, whereas an unequal split of 2% for T-DXd versus THP and 3% for T-DXd plus pertuzumab versus THP was implemented. Nevertheless, the interim PFS result for T-DXd plus pertuzumab versus THP crossed a very stringent efficacy boundary, so the conclusion would remain statistically robust even under an equal 2.5% split. The interim PFS spending approach was amended from an O'Brien-Fleming type approach to Haybittle-Peto, which made the interim success criterion more stringent and reduced the risk of an early false positive, provided the change was implemented prospectively without access to unblinded comparative PFS data. The exploratory comparison of T-DXd plus pertuzumab versus T-DXd for PFS and OS was not included in the multiple testing procedure. All other secondary endpoints and any associated p-values are considered supportive and interpreted descriptively unless they are formally tested within the prespecified hierarchy.

Statistically relevant amendments were implemented before the interim PFS, including updating the target HR assumption, changing the de novo cap, allowing local PIK3CA results for stratification when central data were unavailable, and amending the interim PFS boundary from an O'BrienFleming type approach to Haybittle-Peto to apply a more stringent interim efficacy criterion, with these changes stated to have been made under maintained sponsor blinding.

## Amendments

Several statistically relevant protocol amendments were implemented after recruitment started and before the interim PFS DCO. These included updating key design assumptions such as the target HR to 0.70 and corresponding interim analyses, changing the de novo cap from 50% to 60%, and allowing local PIK3CA results for eligibility and stratification when central data were unavailable. The interim PFS boundary method was amended from an O'Brien-Fleming type approach to Haybittle-Peto to apply a more stringent interim efficacy threshold, and several secondary endpoint details were streamlined or moved to the SAP. None of these amendments were considered to have an impact on the integrity of the study data.

## Disposition and protocol deviations

1703 patients were screened of which 1157 were randomized 1:1:1. For the large majority of the non-randomised the reason was screen failure (511 [93%]). The reasons for screen failure have been disclosed. The reasons were diverse and are considered pertinent.

In the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm, 33 patients (8.7%) initiated trastuzumab after discontinuation from T-DXd. In the SoC arm the taxane of choice was docetaxel in 64.6% of patients, while paclitaxel was given in 34.4% of patients. At DCO (26 February 2025), overall 45.8% in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm and 33.4% in the THP arm were still ongoing treatment. There was 40.3% in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm still receiving treatment with T-DXd, while 7.7% in the THP arm was still receiving a taxane (docetaxel or paclitaxel).

The main reasons for discontinuation of T-DXd was either adverse event (20.8%, n=79) or progressive disease (21.3%, n= 81) for patients receiving T-DXd + pertuzumab. Discontinuation of a taxane was due to adverse event in 27% (n=99) and due to progression in 19.5% (n=72) in the THP arm. The MAH has sufficiently clarified that the imbalance due to 'other' is largely explained by the planned completion of the chemotherapy component i.e. explained by differences in regimen design and not an unexplained higher rate of treatment discontinuations in the THP arm. Overall,

There was a small number of protocol deviations in complying with the eligibility criteria and the proportion of subjects with deviations was generally balanced in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm and the THP arm, and it is not considered likely that these deviations could have impacted the study results significantly.

## Efficacy data and additional analyses

## Demographics/baseline disease characteristics

The patient population predominantly included Asian patients (50.1%), followed by White patients (36.9%). There were 21.4% patients from Europe and North America. The median age of the patients was 54.0 years (Min - Max: 20 to 85 years). 100% of patients were female. The results from the pivotal trial DB-09 are considered extrapolatable to men with HER2 positive unresectable or metastatic breast cancer based on the common biological and pharmacological rationale and in line with previous EMA decisions for T-DXd and other HER2-targeted treatments (e.g. trastuzumab). With regards to stratification factors recorded at randomisation by IRT system, 52.9% of the ITT had de novo BC and 47.1% had recurrent BC, 55.9% of the ITT had hormone receptor-positive disease (either ER and/or PgR positive), 30.3% of the ITT had a PI3K mutation detected.

## Other disease characteristics

Invasive ductal carcinoma was the predominant histology in the ITT (44.4%). The majority had ECOG performance status 0 (65.2%). The metastatic sites included visceral metastases ( 71.3%), bone and locomotor (38.4%), distant lymph node (32.1%), breast (18.3%), and brain metastases (6.0%) (data not shown). Overall disease characteristics were balanced across treatment arms and considered to reflect the disease characteristics of the target population sufficiently.

## Prior therapy

46.9% of the ITT had received some prior treatment modality. Approximately ≈ 20% of patients in all treatment arms received cytotoxic chemotherapy (e.g. taxanes, anthracyclines, and cyclophosphamide) in both adjuvant (23.0%) and neo-adjuvant settings (20.9%). 13.6% and 23.2% had received trastuzumab in the neoadjuvant and adjuvant setting respectively, while 4.9% and 3.8% had received pertuzumab in the neoadjuvant and adjuvant setting respectively. While 20.3% had received hormonal therapy in the adjuvant setting, very few (approximately 1.3%) had received endocrine therapy in the first line setting alone, as was permitted. While the different prior treatment modalities contribute to a heterogenous population, it is balanced across treatment arms. In a European population, adjuvant treatment in HER2-positive early BC (eBC) with one year of trastuzumab treatment is recommended in addition to chemotherapy and in the neoadjuvant setting trastuzumab and pertuzumab is recommended in addition to chemotherapy (ESMO guideline on eBC 2023). Therefore, with respect to prior trastuzumab and pertuzumab, the neoadjuvant and adjuvant therapy given in the majority of the ITT with recurrent BC (cytotoxic chemotherapy) does not reflect the current treatment strategy in a European target population.

Of note, only 21.4% of the ITT was from Europe or Northern America. It is acknowledged, that the DB-09 study was initiated 2 years prior to the adoption of the ESMO guideline on eBC (2023), which recommends trastuzumab and pertuzumab in the adjuvant setting. In addition, the eligibility criteria select an a priori heterogenous population, due to the inclusion of patients with either recurrent or de novo mBC.

## Primary endpoint results

At IA1 (DCO: 26 February 2025) and with a maturity of 37.6% the DB-09 study met one part of the dual primary endpoints by showing a PFS superiority for T-DXd + pertuzumab over THP. The PFS HR was 0.56 (95% CI: 0.44, 0.71; p &lt; 0.00001). A total of 118 patients (30.8%) in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm and 172 patients (44.4%) in the THP arm experienced progression or had died without progression. The median PFS by BICR was longer in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm (40.7 months, 95% CI: 36.5, NC) compared with THP arm (26.9 months, 95% CI: 21.8, NC). A preplanned supplemental analysis applying the 2 missed visits censoring rule (as required per the EMA Guideline on Missing Data in Confirmatory Clinical Trials) showed a HR 0.56 (95% CI 0.45,0.70). Also, a pre-planned ancillary analysis which counts initiation of subsequent cancer therapy as an event, showed a supportive HR of HR 0.57 (95% CI; 0.44-0.73). The median duration of follow-up for censored patients was 27.60 months in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm and 25.10 months in the THP arm. At approximately 4 months, a sustained separation of the KM curves in favour of T-DXd + pertuzumab was observed.

## Secondary endpoint results

PFS by investigator was a secondary endpoint. At DCO, there were 126 events (32.9%) in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm and 208 events (53.7%) in the THP arm. The HR was 0.49 (95% CI: 0.39-0.61). The event difference between BICR and INV was 2.1 % in the T-DXD + pertuzumab arm and 9.3% in the THP arm, which could indicate investigator bias in favour of the experimental arm, however, since the primary endpoint is BICR controlled, this potential bias has no consequence for the integrity of the study results.

OS was not multiplicity controlled. At IA1, the overall OS maturity was 16.3%, and there were 58 deaths (15.1%) in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm and 68 deaths (17.6%) in the THP arm, respectively. The median OS follow-up duration was 29.47 months (range: 0.03, 44.45 months) in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm and 28.85 months (range: 0.07, 44.68 months) in the THP arm. No sound conclusions on OS can be drawn at this level of maturity, however, there is no trend towards a detrimental effect in the experimental arm and a potential detrimental effect on OS is considered unlikely. The MAH committed to provide results from the final OS analysis post-approval (REC).

At IA1, a numerical improvement in PFS2 was observed in favour of T-DXd + pertuzumab compared with THP (79 events, 20.6% vs 115 events, 29.7%; HR: 0.60, 95% CI: 0.45, 0.79; nominal p-value: 0.00038). The median PFS2 was not reached in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm, while it was 36.5 months (95% CI: 36.1, NC) in the THP arm. In light of the immature OS analysis, the PFS2 results indicate that a detriment in OS is unlikely.

The secondary endpoints (ORR per BICR and DoR) can be considered nominally supportive of the primary endpoint.

## Subgroups for PFS by BICR

Analyses for the primary endpoint (PFS by BICR) were conducted for pre-defined subgroups for T-DXd + pertuzumab vs THP. With the exception of one subgroup (age ≥65 years, 18.2% of ITT), all hazard ratios were consistently below 0.67 and with 95% CI predominantly below 1. Of note, the subgroup analysis for geographical region Europe and North America showed an HR of 0.60 (0.35 - 1.01) and prior exposure to anti-HER2 therapies showed an HR of 0.55 (95% CI 0.36-0.83), which is reassuring in light of the heterogenous prior treatment characteristics of the population. Efficacy appeared to be better in de novo BC (HR: 0.49) than in recurrent BC (HR: 0.63). An improvement in PFS was seen irrespective of PI3K mutation status and HR receptor status.

## 2.4.4. Conclusions on the clinical efficacy

At the first interim analysis (DCO: 26 February 2025), the DB-09 study met one part of the dual primary endpoint, PFS by BICR, showing a clinically meaningful and statistically significant improvement in PFS for T-DXd + pertuzumab versus THP in the first line setting of HER2-positive advanced and metastatic breast cancer (HR: 0.56; 95% CI: 0.44, 0.71). The median follow-up was approximately 26 months. Overall survival data were immature (with 16.3% maturity). Although being heterogenous, the ITT overall reflects the target population for which the indication is sought, however with some deviations. The proportion of patients treated with HER2-targeted therapy in the neoadjuvant and adjuvant setting was low, and thus the majority of the ITT was not aligned with the current treatment practice in Europe. Other secondary endpoints (PFS by INV, PFS2, ORR and DoR), although only nominally tested, were supportive of the primary endpoint.

## 2.5. Clinical safety

## Introduction

The primary analysis of the safety and tolerability of T-DXd in support of the proposed indication is based on data from study DB-09, which enrolled patients with HER2-positive, advanced or metastatic BC.

The Safety Analysis Set included 381 patients who received T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg + pertuzumab (T-DXd + pertuzumab arm), and 382 patients who received THP (THP arm) (see below table).

The overall safety data for T-DXd at a dose of 5.4 mg/kg are also summarised based on pooled data sets that include supportive studies in BC (the T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg BC Pool [representing the established safety profile of T-DXd] and the T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg + Pertuzumab BC Pool [referred to as the T-DXd + pertuzumab Pool]) and in a variety of other tumor types (the T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg All Tumor Types Pool [referred to as the T-DXd ATT Pool]).

a Total (or intended) treatment duration was calculated as the number of months from date A to date B (ie, B-A + 1)/30.4375, where A is the date of first dose of the study drug in the dosing period. B is the earliest of: the date of death, the date of DCO, and the date when the last non-zero dose of the study drug was received (eg,&gt; 0 mg of T-DXd) plus C, where C was equal to scheduled number of days between doses - 1.

For overall exposure, A is the date of first dose of any study drug in the dosing period and B was the earliest of: the date of death, the date of DCO, and the date when the last non-zero dose of any study drug was received plus C, where C was equal to scheduled number of days between doses - 1.

b Actual treatment duration = intended treatment duration – total duration of dose delays, where intended exposure will be calculated as in a. Total duration of dose delays = sum for all dosing dates of positive values of [date of the dose – date of the previous dose – (C + 2) days], where C was equal to scheduled

number of days between doses.

Rows were cumulative and patients were included if they had taken treatment up to that number of months.

## Adverse Drug Reactions (ADRs)

Study DB-09 provided the primary clinical safety data for the evaluation and the assessment of the ADR determination in the target population. TEAEs, laboratory data, and vital signs from study DB-09 were comprehensively reviewed by the MAH with relevant safety data from non-clinical studies, and other clinical studies, along with adverse events of special interest (AESIs) (ILD/ pneumonitis and LV dysfunction) for the target population. The totality of the available safety information was considered, and clinical judgment was applied. ADRs included in the T-DXd, pertuzumab, and THP approved indications and other medical concepts that were expected based on the class of drug were systematically reviewed. Other sources included data from the studies that comprised the T-DXd BC Pool and T-DXd All Tumor Types Pool. Events that had already been identified as T-DXd BC ADRs continued to be ADRs. Pertuzumab ADRs were derived from the available pertuzumab label. This was subjected to individual assessment based on frequency and severity of the events and/or evaluation of confounding factors.

It Vision blurred (grouped term) includes PTs of Vision blurred, Visual impairment.

- ² Pancytopenia was defined as all 3 criteria of Haemoglobin level &lt; 100 g/L, Neutrophils &lt; 1.5*10^9/L, and Platelets &lt; 100*10^9/L met on the same lab sample collection date and/or PT of Pancytopenia.

With regards to the minor changes included in section 4.8 of the SmPC for the T-DXd monotherapy 5.4mg/kg, the minor differences in frequencies observed for the monotherapy 5.4mg/kg T-DXd ATT Pool (N=3057) are due to the use of different data cut-off (DCO) dates between the 2 latest applications for Enhertu (EMA/VR/0000322236 EOI (based on study DB-09) and EMA/VR/0000293327 EOI (based on the DP-02 study)). While the total number of patients remains the same across submissions (N = 3057), the varying DCOs result in a slightly different number of events being captured. As a consequence of the updated T-DXd ATT Pool, the frequency of the ADR 'infusion-related reactions' has been revised in section 4.8 of the SmPC from 'uncommon' to 'common'.

a Non-missing n is the number of patients with both baseline and post-baseline data. Percentages were calculated using the non-missing n as denominator.

b ≥ 90% baseline since worst grade is defined as the highest post-baseline LVEF after the measurement with worst grade that is ≥ 90% of the baseline LVEF value.

c Percentages were calculated using the number of patients having worst post-baseline at the specific grade. If there are no LVEF measurements after the worst grade ofLVEF, the patient is not included in the denominator.

The baseline value is defined as the last non-missing value before initial administration of study drug.

Per CTCAE, Grade 2 LVEF decrease is defined by a resting ejection fraction of ≥ 40% to &lt; 50%, or a 10% to &lt; 20% decrease from baseline. Grade 3 LVEF decrease is defined by a resting ejection fraction of≥ 20% to &lt;4 0%, or a ≥ 20% decrease from baseline. Grade 4 LVEF decrease is defined by a resting ejection fraction of &lt; 20%.

If relationship was missing, the AE was also considered to be related to T-DXd.

A TEAE is defined as an AE that occurs, having been absent before the first dose of study drug, or worsens in severity or seriousness after initiating study drug up until 47 days (28 days for J101, 90 days for DL03) after last dose of the study drug. In DP01, DP02, DL03, DL05, DB06, DB07 and DB09, related SAEs after the safety follow-up or any AEs after the first subsequent cancer therapy are not considered as TEAE. For other studies in the pooling, relates SAEs and AEs after the first subsequent cancer therapy are considered as TEAE. Please refer to individual SAPs for more details.

For related TEAE, TEAE leading to drug discontinuation/interruption/reduction, only those regarding to T-DXd were summarized.

## Safety related to drug-drug interactions and other interactions

No interactions with strong cytochrome P450 3A and organic anion transporting polypeptide 1B inhibitors were observed in a dedicated drug-drug interaction study (DS8201-A-A104) with ritonavir and itraconazole in subjects with BC.

No new information on drug interactions is available since the time of study DS8201-A-A104 (submitted as part of EMEA/H/C/005124/0000).

## Post marketing experience

Cumulatively, since the first approval of T-DXd on 20 December 2019 through 19 December 2024 (the DCO of the latest PBRER), the estimated cumulative post-marketing patient exposure was 80,768.5 patient years. During the latest reporting period (20 June 2024 to 19 December 2024), no new data became available that would impact the benefit-risk assessment for T-DXd. No new safety signals have been identified based on post-marketing safety reports. No post-marketing data are available for the proposed therapeutic regimen of T-DXd + pertuzumab, as this is the first combination product being submitted.

## 2.5.1. Discussion on clinical safety

The overall safety assessment of T-DXd + pertuzumab combination therapy is based on the T-DXd + pertuzumab BC safety pool (n=431), including primarily patients from the pivotal study DESTINY-Breast09 (DB-09) coupled with a smaller subset of patients from the ongoing DESTINYBreast07 study (DB-07), Part 2. This safety pool included patients with metastatic BC, who have been exposed to T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg + pertuzumab Q3W as primary therapy for their metastatic disease reflecting the applied extension of indication for Enhertu. The median duration of treatment in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm of the pivotal study DB-09 was 21.65 months and the majority of patients received T-DXd + pertuzumab for more than 6 months (86.6%) with a substantial number of patients receiving treatment for over 12 (72.2%) and 24 months (43.6%) with similar proportions in the T-DXd + pertuzumab BC pool. The safety database for T-DXd + pertuzumab combination therapy is considered relevant and adequate in size, while providing T-DXd + pertuzumab treatment of acceptable duration and dose intensity for safety evaluation.

The safety profiles of the two individual products T-DXd and pertuzumab are both generally known to be acceptable and are considered overall manageable with the greatest risks being interstitial

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

lung disease (ILD)/pneumonitis and left ventricular dysfunction (LVD), which are both important identified risk in the RMP, and infusion-related reactions.

Overall, almost all patients in both the T-DXd + pertuzumab and the THP (i.e., control arm with trastuzumab, pertuzumab and a taxane) arm of study DB-09, and in the T-DXd + pertuzumab BC pool experienced at least one adverse event (AE).

The most common AEs in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm were gastrointestinal and haematological toxicity ADRs, which are known and already included in the Enhertu and Perjeta SmPC, respectively.

The gastrointestinal AEs in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm included nausea (75.1%), vomiting (46.2%), constipation (32.5%) and decreased appetite (32.3%), all seen at least twice as often in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm compared to the THP arm. The level of diarrhoea was similar (63.8% vs 61.5%), but considerably higher than reported for T-DXd monotherapy (T-DXd safety pools ~31%). The haematological AEs seen commonly in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm included neutropenia (grouped term: 50.4% vs 47.1% in the THP arm), anaemia (grouped term: 40.4% vs 46.9% in the THP arm), thrombocytopenia (grouped term: 26.0% vs 6.0% in the THP arm), leukopenia (grouped term: 31.0% vs 32.7% in the THP arm) and lymphopenia (13.9% vs 6.5% in the THP arm). The majority of gastrointestinal AEs resolved and only few reduced doses or discontinuation of treatment were required. In comparison, a substantial part of the haematological AEs did not resolve and up to a third of the patients had reduced or delayed doses while very few discontinued treatments. This is however still in line with the incidences observed for the T-DXd BC and ATT pools.

Additional common ADRs reported in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm included hypokalaemia (grouped term: 28.3% vs 12.0% in the THP arm), transaminases increased (grouped term: 41.5% vs 27.7% in the THP arm), fatigue (grouped term: 53.3% vs 42.1% in the THP arm), decreased weight (29.9% vs 11.3% in the THP arm) and alopecia (48.0% vs 52.6% in the THP arm). Pneumonia was included as an additional ADR for the T-DXd + pertuzumab combination therapy during the evaluation.

The number of patients reporting an AE of grade ≥3 was similar (63.5% vs. 62.3%) in the two arms and somewhat higher than reported for T-DXd monotherapy (T-DXd safety pools ~55%). The most common grade ≥3 AEs reported in both arms were haematological, including neutropenia (24.9% vs 34.6%) and anaemia (10.2% vs 4.5%). Grade ≥3 hypokalaemia was more often seen in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm compared to the THP arm (14.2% vs. 2.6%). Other common grade ≥3 AEs resembled the general common toxicities for the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm.

Serious Adverse Events (SAEs) occurred at similar level in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm (27.0%) and the THP arm (25.1%) and levels were comparable with the T-DXd safety pools (24-28%). The most common SAEs in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm concerned diarrhoea (2.1%), pneumonia (1.8%), febrile neutropenia (1.8%), hypokalaemia (1.8%) and vomiting (1.3%).

A higher proportion of deaths were related to AEs in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm (3.4%, n=13) compared to the THP arm (0.8%, n=3).

In the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm, the most common causes of on-treatment death due to AEs were pneumonia (1.0%, n=4) and sepsis (0.5%, n=2). Pneumonitis, septic shock, febrile neutropenia, dyspnoea, intestinal ischemia, acute kidney injury and pulmonary embolism counted for one case each. Causes of death in the THP arm were anaemia, hepatitis and fall, one case each. Overall, death causes in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm were primarily of an infectious nature, preceded in several cases by (febrile) neutropenia. The haematological toxicity profile of the T-DXd + pertuzumab combination thus appears to be more severe than in the THP arm. The current

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

recommendations in sections 4.2 and 4.4 of the Enhertu SmPC including dose interruption or reduction and monitoring of complete blood counts are considered sufficient also for the T-DXd + pertuzumab combination.

AEs of Special Interest (AESIs) included ILD/pneumonitis and left ventricular dysfunction (LVD).

Adjudicated ILD/pneumonitis cases were found in 12.6% (n=48) of patients in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm vs 1.0% (n=4) in the THP arm. In the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm, 4.5% were Grade 1, 7.6% were Grade 2 and 0.5% (n=2) were Grade 5. Besides two cases of adjudicated ILD/pneumonitis Grade 2 which were not drug-related, all other cases were found to be drugrelated. For 6.0% of patients in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm, the adjudicated drug-related ILD resulted in study drug discontinuation, for 6.6% in drug interruption and for 3.7% in dose reduction. The duration of the first ILD event (median 60.5 days) was comparable to the duration of the first ILD event in the T-DXd safety pools (data not shown). At the time of DCO, a total of 30/48 (62.5%) patients in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm had recovered, 2/48 (4.2%) were recovering, and 14/48 (29.2%) had not recovered. Incidence, severity and outcomes were comparable with the findings in the T-DXd safety pools and thus do not raise new safety concerns. The current warning for ILD/pneumonitis in section 4.4 of the SmPC was updated to reflect that cases of fatal pneumonia were observed, including two cases adjudicated as ILD. The current dose modifications for adverse reactions recommendations in section 4.2 of the SmPC are deemed appropriate.

Based on the selected PTs, 11.0% (n=42) of patients in the TXd + pertuzumab arm experienced LVD, primarily of Grade 1-2 (8.9%, n=34), with Grade 3 in 1.8% (n=7) and Grade 4 in 0.3% (n=1, also reported as an SAE) of patients. No cases were fatal. A lower frequency of LV dysfunction was found in the THP arm and the T-DXd safety pools (~6-7%), with especially fewer cases of Grade &gt;3 LVD (~0.5% in the T-DXd safety pools vs 2.1% in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm and 1.8% in the THP arm). The majority of patients had recovered by the DCO (73.8%), while 21.4% had not recovered. In the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm, the LVD PTs included ejection fraction decreased (8.4%, n=32), left ventricular dysfunction (1.3%, n=5), cardiac failure (1.3%, n=5) and cardiac failure chronic (0.3%, n=1) (data not shown). Overall, the incidences of both All-grade LVD, Grade 3-4 LVD and discontinuations due to LVD were slightly higher in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm compared to the T-DXd monotherapy assessed in the T-DXd safety pools. Among the patients with ECHO/MUGA scans performed after the measurement of worst-grade LVEF, recovery of (the few) patients in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm experiencing a Grade 3 event was much lower than in the T-DXd safety pools (2/11, 18.2% vs 10/16, ~62%). These findings are not surprising considering the concurrent treatment with pertuzumab. According to the Perjeta SmPC, patients with metastatic BC should have a pre-treatment LVEF of &gt;50%, while patients who have received prior anthracyclines or prior radiotherapy to the chest area may be at higher risk of LVEF declines.

## Special populations

Subgroup-analyses of AEs concerning intrinsic and extrinsic factors revealed a more severe safety profile among patients &gt;65 years compared to patients &lt;65 years (this is adequately reflected in section 4.8 of the SmPC) and patients with mild hepatic impairment (higher rates of Grade ≥3 AEs compared to patients with normal hepatic function). The latter is considered a chance finding.

Discontinuation of treatment due to AEs was seen in 20.7% in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm and in 28.3% in the THP arm. The primary cause of discontinuation due to AEs in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm was ILD/pneumonitis (6.6%), whilst only accounting for one case (0.3%) in the THP arm, however in the range of the frequencies observed in the T-DXd safety pools.

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

Inclusion of the proposed ADRs for the T-DXd + pertuzumab combination therapy in section 4.8 of the SmPC, is endorsed. All identified ADRs for the combination treatment had already been described for the monotherapy, except for 'mucosal inflammation' which has been added for the combination treatment with a frequency 'common'.

## 2.5.2. Conclusions on clinical safety

The safety profile of the T-DXd + pertuzumab combination as first-line treatment in patients with HER2-positive metastatic BC is generally comparable to the known safety profile of T-DXd monotherapy in patients with BC and other tumours. Toxicities of the T-DXd + pertuzumab combination were mostly gastrointestinal (nausea, vomiting, constipation) and haematological (neutropenia, anaemia, thrombocytopenia, pancytopenia).

ILD/pneumonitis continues to be the most important identified risk of T-DXd, and while the incidence of ILD/pneumonitis in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm was higher (12.6%) than the THP arm (1.0%), it was comparable to T-DXd monotherapy (T-DXd safety pools ~13%).

Conclusively, the safety profile of the T-DXd + pertuzumab combination treatment shows nonnegligible toxicity primarily of gastrointestinal and haematological character, which is known and considered overall manageable.

## 2.7.1. User consultation

A justification for not performing a full user consultation with target patient groups on the package leaflet has been submitted by the MAH and has been found acceptable for the following reasons:

1. In accordance with articles 59(3) and 61(1) of Directive 2001/83/EC, the MAH completed a full user test of the PIL during the review of the initial Marketing Authorisation Application (MAA) for Enhertu (EMEA/H/C/005124/0000)
2. Enhertu is prescribed by a physician and administered intravenously under the supervision of a healthcare professional at a hospital/clinic setting. The posology, administration and method of reconstitution for the extension of indication is unchanged.
3. The updates to the PIL, including the safety sections, are not significant and utilise well recognised lay terms. Furthermore, the PL will be kept identical in format size, colours, layout/design as illustrated in the agreed mock-ups.

## 3. Benefit-Risk Balance

## 3.1. Therapeutic Context

## 3.1.1. Disease or condition

The recommended indication reflecting the data evaluated is:

Enhertu in combination with pertuzumab is indicated for the first-line treatment of adult patients with unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer (for biomarker-based patient selection, see section 4.2).

## 3.1.2. Available therapies and unmet medical need

HER2-positive breast cancer comprises approximately 20% of all breast cancers (Wolff et al. 2018, Arteaga et al. 2011). Unresectable and metastatic HER2-positive (IHC3+ or ISH+) breast cancer remains an incurable disease. The standard of care in the first line treatment of HER-2 positive unresectable or metastatic breast cancer is pertuzumab in combination with trastuzumab and a taxane (docetaxel or other taxane) (ESMO guideline 2021, Gennari et al. 2021). This regime is recommended in the first-line setting regardless of hormone receptor (HR) status (ER and/or PgR). For patients with HR-positive and HER2-positive tumours, endocrine therapy (ET) may be added to trastuzumab and pertuzumab as maintenance therapy after completing at least six cycles of concomitant chemotherapy (ESMO guideline 2021). Patients with HER2-positive mBC will ultimately develop treatment resistance and run out of effective treatments.

## 3.1.3. Main clinical studies

The current application is based on a single pivotal study DESTINY-Breast09 (DB-09): a phase III, open-label, randomised, 3-arm, global study comparing trastuzumab-deruxtecan (T-DXd) with or without pertuzumab (blinded for pertuzumab in the T-DXd arms) compared with THP (taxane, trastuzumab and pertuzumab) as first-line treatment in patients with HER2-positive, unresectable, or metastatic breast cancer. Eligible patients had either de novo mBC or recurrent BC. Prior treatment in the neoadjuvant or adjuvant setting was permitted, with a disease-free interval (DFI) from completion of systemic chemotherapy or HER2-targeted therapy to advanced or metastatic

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

diagnosis of at least 6 months. Patients could be either HR-positive or HR-negative and must have ECOG performance status 0-1.

1157 patients were randomized 1:1:1 at 279 centres in 27 countries. The presented data are from the first interim analysis (IA) at the DCO of 26 February 2025. The primary endpoint PFS was dual, aiming at establishing 1) the superiority of T-DXd compared to THP and/or 2) the superiority of T-DXd + pertuzumab compared to THP. OS was to be tested hierarchically, only if both primary PFS comparisons were significant. The comparison between the T-DXd monotherapy arm and the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm is only planned to be an exploratory comparison.

The patient population predominantly included Asian patients (50.0%). There were 21.7% patients from Europe and North America.

## 3.2. Favourable effects

At IA1 (DCO: 26 February 2025) and with a maturity of 37.6% the DB-09 study met one part of the dual primary endpoints by showing a clinically meaningful and statistically significant PFS benefit for T-DXd + pertuzumab over THP. The PFS HR was 0.56 (95% CI: 0.44, 0.71; p &lt; 0.00001). The median PFS by BICR was 40.7 months (95% CI: 36.5, NC) in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm and 26.9 months (95% CI: 21.8, NC) in the THP arm. A pre-planned supplemental analysis applying the 2 missed visits censoring rule showed a HR 0.56 (95% CI: 0.45, 0.70).

The pre-planned subgroup analyses were overall consistent with the primary endpoint result. Particularly the subgroup analysis for geographical region Europe and North America showed an HR of 0.60 (95% CI: 0.35, 1.01) and prior exposure to anti-HER2 therapies showed an HR of 0.55 (95% CI: 0.36, 0.83), which is reassuring in light of the heterogenous prior treatment characteristics of the population. An improvement in PFS was seen irrespective of PI3K mutation status and HR receptor status.

At IA1 the overall OS maturity was 16.3%, and there were 58 deaths (15.1%) in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm and 68 deaths (17.6%) in the THP arm. The median OS follow-up duration was 29.47 months (range: 0.03, 44.45 months) in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm and 28.85 months (range: 0.07, 44.68 months) in the THP arm. The primary endpoint was overall supported by numerical benefits in the secondary endpoints ORR, DoR, PFS2 (not multiplicity controlled).

## 3.3. Uncertainties and limitations about favourable effects

- No sound conclusions on OS can be drawn at this level of maturity; however, there is no trend towards a detrimental effect in the experimental arm. The MAH will provide results of the final OS analysis post-approval (REC).
- The comparison between the T-DXd monotherapy arm and the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm is only planned to be an exploratory comparison and not included in the multiple testing procedure. Thus, the contribution of the components of the T-DXd + pertuzumab vs T-DXd monotherapy, cannot be formally disentangled.

## 3.4. Unfavourable effects

The overall safety assessment of T-DXd + pertuzumab combination therapy is based on the T-DXd + pertuzumab BC safety pool (n=431), including primarily patients from the pivotal study DESTINY-Breast09 (DB-09) coupled with a smaller subset of patients from the ongoing DESTINYBreast07 study (DB-07). This safety pool included patients with metastatic BC, who have been

\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_\\_

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

exposed to T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg + pertuzumab Q3W as first-line therapy for their metastatic disease. The median duration of treatment in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm of the pivotal study DB-09 was 21.65 months.

The safety profiles of the two individual substances T-DXd and pertuzumab are both generally known to be acceptable and are considered overall manageable with the greatest risks being interstitial lung disease (ILD)/pneumonitis (which is an important identified risk in the RMP for Enhertu), left ventricular dysfunction (LVD) (which is an important identified risk in the RMP for both Enhertu and Perjeta) and infusion-related reactions (which is an important identified risk in the RMP for Perjeta).

The most common AEs in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm were gastrointestinal (nausea, vomiting, constipation) and haematological (neutropenia, anaemia, thrombocytopenia, pancytopenia) toxicity including ADRs, which are known and already included in the Enhertu and Perjeta SmPC, respectively. The number of patients reporting an AE of grade ≥3 was similar in the two arms (63.5% in the T-DXd + pertuzumab combination arm vs. 62.3% in THP arm) and somewhat higher than reported for T-DXd monotherapy (T-DXd safety pools ~55%). Serious Adverse Events (SAEs) occurred at similar level in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm (27.0%) and the THP arm (25.1%) and comparable with the T-DXd safety pools (24-28%). A higher proportion of deaths were related to AEs in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm (3.4%, n=13) compared to the THP arm (0.8%, n=3). Overall, death causes in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm were primarily of an infectious nature. The haematological toxicity profile of the T-DXd + pertuzumab combination thus appears to be more severe than in the THP arm. The current recommendations in sections 4.2 and 4.4 of the Enhertu SmPC including dose reductions and monitoring of complete blood counts are considered sufficient also for the T-DXd + pertuzumab combination.

Adjudicated ILD/pneumonitis cases were found in 12.6% (n=48) of patients in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm vs 1.0% (n=4) in the THP arm. In the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm, 4.5% were Grade 1, 7.6% were Grade 2 and 0.5% (n=2) were Grade 5. Incidence, severity and outcomes were comparable with the findings in the T-DXd safety pools and thus do not raise new safety concerns. The current warning for ILD/pneumonitis in section 4.4 of the SmPC was updated to reflect that cases of fatal pneumonia were observed, including two cases adjudicated as ILD. The current dose modifications for adverse reactions recommendations in section 4.2 of the SmPC are deemed appropriate.

Based on the selected PTs, 11.0% (n=42) of patients in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm experienced LVD, primarily of Grade 1-2 (8.9%, n=34), with Grade 3 in 1.8% (n=7) and Grade 4 in 0.3% (n=1, also reported as an SAE) of patients. A lower frequency of LV dysfunction was found in the THP arm and the T-DXd safety pools (~6-7%). These findings are not surprising considering the concurrent treatment with pertuzumab.

## 3.5. Uncertainties and limitations about unfavourable effects

None.

## 3.7. Benefit-risk assessment and discussion

## 3.7.1. Importance of favourable and unfavourable effects

At the first interim analysis (DCO: 26 February 2025), the pivotal DB-09 study met one part of the dual primary endpoint, PFS by BICR, showing a clinically meaningful and statistically significant improvement in PFS for the T-DXd + pertuzumab combination versus THP in the first line setting of HER2-positive advanced and metastatic breast cancer (HR: 0.56; 95% CI: 0.44, 0.71). The median follow-up was approximately 26 months.

Overall survival data were immature (with 16.3% maturity). At a median follow-up of approximately 29 months, there were 58 deaths (15.1%) in the T-DXd + pertuzumab arm and 68 deaths (17.6%) in the THP arm. At IA1, a numerical improvement in PFS2 was observed in favour of T-DXd + pertuzumab compared with THP (79 events, 20.6% vs 115 events, 29.7%; HR: 0.60, 95% CI: 0.45, 0.79; nominal p-value: 0.00038). Considering the immature OS analysis, the PFS2 results indicate that a detriment in OS is unlikely. The MAH committed to provide the results of the final OS analysis post-approval (REC).

Although being heterogenous, the ITT population overall reflects the target population for which the indication is sought, however with some deviations. The proportion of patients treated with HER2-targeted therapy in the neoadjuvant and adjuvant setting was low, and thus the majority of the ITT was not aligned with the current treatment practice in Europe. Reassuringly, pre-planned subgroup PFS analyses (also in the European/North American subgroup and in the subgroup with prior HER2-targeted therapy) were consistent with the primary endpoint result. Other secondary endpoints (PFS by INV, PFS2, ORR and DoR), although only nominally tested, were supportive of the primary endpoint. No head-to-head comparison of the T-DXd + pertuzumab and the monotherapy T-DXd arm will be performed, and thus the respective contribution of T-DXd and pertuzumab to treatment efficacy will remain uncertain.

The safety profile of T-DXd + pertuzumab treatment shows non-negligible toxicity primarily of gastrointestinal and haematological character, which is known and considered overall manageable. The major safety concern continues to be the risk of ILD/pneumonitis.

## 3.7.2. Balance of benefits and risks

Unresectable and metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer remains an incurable disease. The current standard of care in the first-line treatment of HER2-positive unresectable or metastatic breast cancer is pertuzumab in combination with trastuzumab and a taxane. Patients will ultimately develop treatment resistance and run out of effective treatments, and thus there is an unmet medical need for more and better treatment options in this disease setting.

Based on the results from the pivotal DB-09 study, T-DXd in combination with pertuzumab for the treatment of adult patients with unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer has demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically relevant benefit in PFS. The safety profile of T-DXd is non-negligible and ILD/pneumonitis remains an important safety concern.

Not applicable.

## 3.8. Conclusions

The overall B/R of Enhertu in the claimed indication is positive.

## 4. Recommendations

## Outcome

Based on the review of the submitted data, the CHMP considers the following variation acceptable and therefore recommends the variation to the terms of the Marketing Authorisation, concerning the following change:

| Variation accepted   | Variation accepted                                                                  | Type              | Annexes affected   |
|----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|--------------------|
| C.I.6.a              | C.I.6.a Addition of a new therapeutic indication or modification of an approved one | Variation type II | I and IIIB         |

Extension of indication for Enhertu in combination with pertuzumab as first-line treatment of adult patients with unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer, based on the results from the DESTINY-Breast09 study, a phase III study of trastuzumab deruxtecan with or without pertuzumab versus THP (taxane, trastuzumab and pertuzumab) as first-line treatment in patients with HER2-positive, unresectable, or metastatic breast cancer. As a consequence, sections 4.1, 4.2, 4.4, 4.8 and 5.1 of the SmPC are updated and the Package Leaflet is updated in accordance. Version 12.0 of the RMP has also been agreed.

## Amendments to the marketing authorisation

In view of the data submitted with the variation, amendments to Annexes I and IIIB and to the Risk Management Plan are recommended.
